chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.sourcePressure: Define deep work and shallow work, then state the deep-work hypothesis from the frozen source bundle.
chapters.coreMove: Separate the tasks that require uninterrupted cognition from the tasks that merely keep you visibly occupied.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating focus as a general preference for fewer distractions.

chapters.title: Deep Work Is Valuable
chapters.sourcePressure: Deep work helps people learn hard things quickly and produce at high quality and quantity.
chapters.coreMove: Identify where rapid learning and high-quality output create the real advantage, then protect attention there first.
chapters.commonMisread: Saying focus is nice because it helps you get more done.

chapters.title: Deep Work Is Rare
chapters.sourcePressure: Modern organizations often reward shallow behaviors through constant connectivity and visible busyness.
chapters.coreMove: Notice when an organization rewards responsiveness instead of contribution, then stop mistaking the signal for the work.
chapters.commonMisread: Complaining that meetings and messages are annoying.

chapters.title: Deep Work Is Meaningful
chapters.sourcePressure: Deep work is intrinsically satisfying and supports a more meaningful work life.
chapters.coreMove: Choose depth as a way to make work more satisfying by giving attention to something worth shaping well.
chapters.commonMisread: Claiming meaningful work means following passion or loving every task.

chapters.title: Work Deeply
chapters.sourcePressure: Scheduling philosophies, rituals, and shutdown routines help create regular depth.
chapters.coreMove: Convert a wish to focus into a calendar, ritual, and shutdown rule that make depth repeatable.
chapters.commonMisread: Telling the reader to block time and try harder.

chapters.title: Embrace Boredom
chapters.sourcePressure: Concentration must be trained; schedule distraction instead of waiting for focus to appear.
chapters.coreMove: Train the mind to stay with a chosen problem by deciding when distraction is allowed before the urge arrives.
chapters.commonMisread: Equating boredom with rest, meditation, or doing nothing.

chapters.title: Quit Social Media
chapters.sourcePressure: Use a craftsman mindset and keep only tools that substantially support what matters.
chapters.coreMove: Judge each network tool by whether its concrete benefits substantially outweigh the attention it costs.
chapters.commonMisread: Making a blanket moral case against social media.

chapters.title: Drain the Shallows
chapters.sourcePressure: Reduce shallow obligations, constrain email sprawl, and defend time for deep work.
chapters.coreMove: Quantify shallow obligations, cap them deliberately, and redesign communication so depth has room to happen.
chapters.commonMisread: Telling readers to ignore email or become unavailable.

chapters.title: Conclusion
chapters.sourcePressure: The supported closing case is Bill Gates as an example of the value of a deep life.
chapters.coreMove: Treat depth as a life design choice that must be chosen repeatedly, not as a single productivity tactic.
chapters.commonMisread: Ending with a generic summary that repeats all four rules.
